pac: Pac times CATCH release so the returning sac is caught on PARCEL and then takes the lower exit; this role is active again if the first release is early.

common_mistakes.mistake: Release Pac from CATCH before the outbound sac clears the receiver gate.
common_mistakes.consequence: The gate stops the parcel before the receiver; neither exit gate opens.
common_mistakes.recovery: Step back onto CATCH and repeat the return cycle; this is explicit in the authored hint and is a local retry, not an irreversible loss.

confirmed: The first-pass concern about a one-way/return timing relationship is directionally correct: CATCH must be released after the outbound parcel passes so PARCEL catches its return.

incorrect_inferences: The idle first-pass phrase “one-way” may imply an irreversible delivery. Actual source makes it a repeatable boomerang loop with a retryable receiver gate.
changed_judgments: Timing becomes a known ordered, repeatable gate interaction (2), rather than unknown. Hazards becomes 0 and recovery 1 because the source explicitly supplies a safe floor and local retry. Novelty decreases from 3 to 2 because level 25 already taught the delivery/return-sac concept; the timed receiver catch is the new combination.
unresolved: There is no retained ordinary-input route artifact for level 33; actual input timing, Pac jump precision, human cue-reading, and how quickly a new pair discovers the “step off after passage” rule remain unmeasured.

single_operator_note: The estimates assume two people, one per hero. One operator must interleave distinct Isp A/D/W and Pac arrow-key inputs; simultaneous role work, especially holding a pad while moving the other hero, adds coordination burden. Software key mappings are distinct; physical keyboard rollover and human comfort were not tested.
